questions.question: What is system software?
questions.explanation: System software controls and manages computer hardware.

questions.question: Which is an example of system software?
questions.explanation: Operating systems are core system software.

questions.question: What does a compiler do?
questions.explanation: Compiler converts full source code into machine code.

questions.question: What does an interpreter do?
questions.explanation: Interpreter executes code line by line.

questions.question: Assembler converts:
questions.explanation: Assembler converts assembly language into machine code.

questions.question: Which is not system software?
questions.explanation: MS Excel is application software.

questions.question: Linker is used for:
questions.explanation: Linker combines multiple object files into one executable.

questions.question: Loader is used for:
questions.explanation: Loader places program into memory for execution.

questions.question: Device driver is:
questions.explanation: Device drivers allow OS to communicate with hardware.

questions.question: What is firmware?
questions.explanation: Firmware is software embedded in hardware devices.

questions.question: System calls are used for:
questions.explanation: System calls allow programs to request OS services.

questions.question: Kernel is:
questions.explanation: Kernel manages system resources.

questions.question: Which software controls CPU scheduling?
questions.explanation: Operating system handles CPU scheduling.

questions.question: What is a shell?
questions.explanation: Shell allows users to interact with OS.

questions.question: Which tool finds errors in code?
questions.explanation: Debugger helps identify and fix errors.

questions.question: Which software manages memory?
questions.explanation: Operating system manages memory allocation.

questions.question: High-level language is converted to machine code by:
questions.explanation: Compiler translates high-level code to machine code.

questions.question: What is utility software?
questions.explanation: Utilities help maintain and optimize system.

questions.question: Which is a system utility?
questions.explanation: Disk cleanup is a system utility.

questions.question: Which part handles I/O operations?
questions.explanation: Operating system manages I/O devices.

questions.question: What does LAN stand for?
questions.explanation: LAN refers to a network within a small geographical area.

questions.question: Which device connects multiple networks?
questions.explanation: Router connects different networks and routes data.

questions.question: What is the full form of IP?
questions.explanation: IP is used for addressing and routing data packets.

questions.question: Which layer is responsible for data encryption?
questions.explanation: Presentation layer handles encryption and formatting.

questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP is used for communication over the web.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to send emails?
questions.explanation: SMTP is used for sending emails.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to receive emails?
questions.explanation: POP3 is used to retrieve emails from server.

questions.question: Which topology connects all nodes to a central hub?
questions.explanation: In star topology, all nodes connect to a central hub.

questions.question: What is the function of a switch?
questions.explanation: Switch sends data to specific destination.

questions.question: Which layer handles routing?
questions.explanation: Network layer determines best path for data.

questions.question: What is bandwidth?
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the rate of data transfer.

questions.question: Which device regenerates signals?
questions.explanation: Repeater strengthens weak signals.

questions.question: What is DNS?
questions.explanation: DNS converts domain names into IP addresses.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for file transfer?
questions.explanation: FTP is used for transferring files.

questions.question: Which layer ensures reliable data delivery?
questions.explanation: Transport layer ensures reliability and error handling.

questions.question: Which address is unique to each device?
questions.explanation: MAC address uniquely identifies a device.

questions.question: Which protocol is connection-oriented?
questions.explanation: TCP ensures reliable connection-based communication.

questions.question: What is a firewall?
questions.explanation: Firewall protects network from unauthorized access.

questions.question: Which topology forms a closed loop?
questions.explanation: Ring topology connects nodes in circular manner.

questions.question: Which network covers large geographical area?
questions.explanation: WAN spans across large geographical areas.

questions.question: What is an operating system?
questions.explanation: OS is system software that manages hardware and software resources.

questions.question: Which is an example of OS?
questions.explanation: Windows is an operating system.

questions.question: What is process?
questions.explanation: A process is an active program in execution.

questions.question: Which scheduling is first come first serve?
questions.explanation: FCFS executes processes in arrival order.

questions.question: Which scheduling uses time slice?
questions.explanation: Round Robin uses time quantum for each process.

questions.question: What is deadlock?
questions.explanation: Deadlock occurs when processes wait indefinitely.

questions.question: Which memory is fastest?
questions.explanation: Cache memory is fastest among these.

questions.question: What is paging?
questions.explanation: Paging divides memory into fixed-size blocks.

questions.question: Which is non-volatile memory?
questions.explanation: ROM retains data even after power off.

questions.question: What is a thread?
questions.explanation: Thread is a smaller unit of a process.

questions.question: Which OS allows multiple users?
questions.explanation: Multi-user OS supports multiple users simultaneously.

questions.question: Which OS works in real-time?
questions.explanation: Real-time OS responds immediately to inputs.

questions.question: What is virtual memory?
questions.explanation: Virtual memory extends RAM using disk storage.

questions.question: Which manages files?
questions.explanation: Operating system manages file system.

questions.question: Which algorithm gives minimum waiting time?
questions.explanation: Shortest Job First minimizes average waiting time.

questions.question: What is kernel?
questions.explanation: Kernel is the central part of OS.

questions.question: Which is not OS function?
questions.explanation: Word processing is application software.

questions.question: What is context switching?
questions.explanation: CPU switches from one process to another.

questions.question: Which scheduling is preemptive?
questions.explanation: Round Robin allows process interruption.

questions.question: Which handles I/O devices?
questions.explanation: Operating system manages I/O operations.
